title: Operational Dependability Orbit — Plan & Tactical Threads
body:
Summary:

This is an operational plan for the Dependability Orbit pilot — a cross-functional initiative to land a repeatable SLO adoption and service-reliability ramp for model-serving features. The Orbit is intentionally small-scope: two customer-facing serving routes (chat-generation and embedding-lookup), with a pilot cadence of 8 weeks. Focus: observable SLOs, fast runbook feedback loops, and a gated roll-forward process for model and infra changes.

Hypothesis:
- If product, serving-runtime, platform, and SRE align on lightweight SLO definitions + deterministic telemetry + a simple rollback policy, then we can reduce high-severity incidents and shorten incident-to-resolution time by 30% on the pilot routes within 8 weeks.

Success criteria (measurable):
- SLOs defined and in telemetry for both routes by week 2.
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for high-severity incidents on pilot routes < 30 minutes for canaryed deploys by week 8.
- Two successful canary rollouts using the Gate-and-Fallback policy without customer-visible errors.
- Post-pilot retrospective with a prioritized backlog of at least 6 repeatable changes (metrics, runbooks, automation).

Scope (what we will deliver):
- SLOs: request latency p95, error rate (user-visible errors), cache-hit ratio for embeddings, and degradation score (composite).
- Telemetry owners: define metrics naming, dashboards, and alert thresholds.
- Runbooks: one primary oncall playbook per route + escalation mapping.
- Canary gating: automated health checks + rollback triggers for 3-minute, 10-minute, 60-minute windows.
- Weekly synchronizations and a decision log to capture tradeoffs.

Out of scope:
- Full-breadth platform-wide SLO rollout (this is a pilot).
- Deep kernel/quantization performance tuning — perf anomalies will be flagged, not fixed in-scope.

Stakeholders & responsibilities:
- Product-hosted-api: Lina Zhao — route owners, customer-impact context, acceptance criteria for canary.
- Serving-runtime: Marco Rivera — instrumentation, canary hook points, KV/Prefix cache telemetry.
- Platform-engineering: Samir Gupta — autoscaling policies, capacity reservations for pilot.
- SRE (this doc owner): Asha Patel — SLO framing, runbook templates, incident retro facilitation.
- Developer-experience: Elena Morris — doc templates, onboarding checklist for feature teams.
- Security/Compliance (consult): Priya Desai — ensure telemetry and logs meet retention/PII guardrails.

Workstreams and tactical threads (parallel):
1) Telemetry & Alerting (owner: Marco)
  - Deliverable: metric names, recording rules, dashboards in observability console.
  - Tasks: add p95 latency, 5xx/4xx flags for user-visible errors, embedding cache-hit metric, composite degradation_score.
  - Short experiment: trial a rolling average smoothing (window=15s) to reduce alert noise.

2) SLO Definition & Verification (owner: Asha + Lina)
  - Deliverable: SLO doc for each route (target, measurement window, error budget policy).
  - Tasks: define business-level indicators (BLIs) vs. technical indicators, set SLOs for canary and production.
  - Decision heuristic: start conservative on targets for canaries (e.g., 98% p95 compliance) and tighten for prod after 2 successful canaries.

3) Runbooks & Oncall Playbooks (owner: Samir)
  - Deliverable: simple step-by-step runbooks with checks for common failure modes (scaling, OOMs, degraded cache).
  - Tasks: map escalation contacts, add runbook links to alert notifications, create a 1-page quick reference.

4) Canary Automation & Rollback (owner: Marco + Platform)
  - Deliverable: Gate-and-Fallback pipeline: automated validation checks, automatic rollback on sustained threshold breach.
  - Tasks: implement health-check traffic splitting, proto-alert to abort if error budget spends > 50% in 30 minutes.

5) Comms & Documentation (owner: Elena)
  - Deliverable: onboarding checklist for participating teams, weekly status notes, and pilot FAQ.

Timeline (8-week pilot):
- Week 0 (planning): finalize stakeholders, confirm pilot routes, reserve capacity, and baseline telemetry.
- Week 1: implement metric instrumentation and SLO drafts.
- Week 2: dashboards live, runbook skeletons, first tabletop run of canary process.
- Week 3–4: dry-run canary (shadow traffic), iterate alerts to reduce false positives.
- Week 5: first canary with limited traffic (5%) — monitor and collect logs/trace.
- Week 6: canary review; if green, perform staged rollout to 25% then 100% with checkpoints.
- Week 7: run simulated failure drills (introduce latency, cache miss storms) and refine runbooks.
- Week 8: pilot retrospective, quantify metrics, and create follow-up backlog.

Key dependencies:
- Observability infra: must support recording rules and composite metrics (team: observability).
- Capacity reservations from Dedicated pools for canary isolation (platform).
- A test harness for synthetic traffic that mirrors customer request shapes (devexp).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Alert fatigue from poorly tuned thresholds. Mitigation: use short shadowing phase for two weeks and use rolling average smoothing before enabling alerts.
- Risk: Canary exposes a critical bug impacting customer data paths. Mitigation: traffic-splitting isolation, canary scale limit (max 5% initially), immediate fallback to stable variant.
- Risk: Missing ownership across teams (blame gap). Mitigation: explicit oncall rota mapping and escalation matrix in runbooks.

Decision log (live):
- 2026-08-04: Adopt composite degradation_score = (normalized p95 latency + error_rate*2 + cache_miss_penalty). Rationale: single signal for automation. Owner: Marco.
- 2026-08-10: Canary threshold: abort rollout if degradation_score > 0.6 for 10 continuous minutes. Owner: Asha.
- 2026-08-12: Alert cadence: suppress p95 alerts during first two minutes of a deploy to avoid transient blips. Owner: Samir.

Open questions / things to validate:
- What is the minimal set of tracing fields needed to quickly attribute origin (model vs infra) for generation routes? (action: Marco to prototype.)
- Can Dedicated autoscaler support sub-second scale-up for sudden traffic spikes? (action: Samir to validate with infra team.)
- What SLO target map should we communicate externally vs internally for the pilot? (action: Lina to draft customer-facing vs internal SLOs).

Immediate next steps (next 5 working days):
- Marco: push first metric PR for p95 latency and cache_hit_count. (due: 2026-08-07)
- Samir: reserve two nodes in dedicated pool and confirm autoscale policy. (due: 2026-08-07)
- Asha: publish SLO template and complete the first version of the decision log. (due: 2026-08-06)
- Elena: create the pilot onboarding doc and short FAQ. (due: 2026-08-09)

Notes-to-self (working doc flavor):
- Keep language pragmatic and avoid over-formalizing SLOs at pilot start. We want fast feedback loops.
- Expect to adapt metric names once debugging shows gaps; keep mapping doc of old -> new names.
- Capture one example incident walk-through during week 6 to validate runbook clarity.

Appendix (links & references):
- Baseline dashboards: OBSERV-3612 (work-in-progress).
- Related Confluence: Dependability Orbit (see linked artifact).
- Template runbooks: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/tree/main/templates
